newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE'S ENAP SIGNS ARGENTINE NATURAL GAS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CHILE'S ENAP SIGNS ARGENTINE NATURAL GAS DEAL.

text.p: Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (Enap) has signed a deal to buy natural gas from fields owned by an Argentine-French group in Argentina's far south.

Enap on Tuesday said it agreed to buy 250,000 tonnes of liquefied natural gas a year under a long-term supply contract with Consorcio Cuenca Marina Austral, which includes Argentina's Dominex and Bridas Energy Corp BDS.N and France's Total SA.

Enap will build a pipeline to bring the gas, a mixture of propane and butane, from gas fields in the Argentine section of the island of Tierra del Fuego across the Straits of Magellan to the company's plant near the city of Punta Arenas.

"This project will reinforce energy integration between Chile and Argentina, as well as with the rest of South America as part of the production will be sold in other markets in the region," said Leon Sougarret, manager of Enap Magallanes, in a statement.
Enap will sell the propane while the butane will be distributed by Total, an Enap spokesman saod.
Construction will begin at the end of the year, and the pipeline should go into operation in late 1998, he said.
The spokesman declined to say how much the project would cost.
